minutes.headline: Select Board approved a cyclist pass-through; discussed ARPA deadlines, FY25 goals, MUNIS replacement and a roof overage.
minutes.summary: The board heard public comment about unfilled records requests, then approved a charity bicycle pass-through. The interim town manager reported on hiring, a roof bid over budget, a Tri-Pasos building account deficit, thin capital funds and ARPA commitment deadlines. Members previewed FY25 goals, discussed workshops, budget guidance, warrants and the MUNIS software problem. No budget figures were set.

public_comment.topic: Resident says public records requests to the interim town manager are unfulfilled and under appeal, concerning a shed on common land, and alleges retaliation and a tax change connected to a board member.

Green Communities vice chair reports work with the school department toward the October grant round for phase two of the mini splits, and raises concern that the draft financial policy manual has no redline against existing policies.

budget_items.what_was_said: Budget was lower than the bid received; the overage must come from the facilities operating budget and the finance committee may need to backfill at town meeting.
A transfer has been requested to cover state inspection services now that there is no local inspector; to be raised with the finance committee.
Program expires end of September; a stop-gap is needed for October and November until fall town meeting.
School committee voted a one-year agreement with an increase, as reported by the interim town manager.
Funds on hand appear woefully short for proposed projects including Ritter windows; money appropriated years ago has lost purchasing power.
The account that operates the building has a deficit because rents go in and bills are paid with no budget, which reduces free cash.
Library concerned committed funds may be recommitted before contract; funds across projects and the teen room specifically.
Cost of windows on one side of the building raised as example.
Interim town manager said he will ask the board for budget guidance (flat, level service, expansion, reduction) before budget season.
Cloud pricing is an uptick; first three years covered by ARPA payroll allocation.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to approve a charity bicycle ride's request to pass through Lunenburg on September 22, 2024.
The interim town manager said the Adult Activity Center roof bid came in over budget; the overage would fall on the facilities operating budget, with a possible backfill at town meeting.

The interim town manager also reported thin building-envelope capital accounts and an operating-account deficit at the Tri-Pasos building, plus a requested transfer for state weights-and-measures inspection.

Members discussed ARPA commitment deadlines, including the library teen room funds, and said the replacement for the MUNIS accounting software is covered by ARPA payroll money for its first three years.
The board set a goals workshop for the next Tuesday, and members have three weeks to comment on the draft financial policy manual.

why_it_matters: The roof overage, the deficit in the Tri-Pasos building account and the transfer for inspection services are costs the town will have to cover from operating budgets or free cash, so they may reach residents as town meeting requests.
The board's FY25 goals and the draft financial policy manual set the budget rules and the guidance (flat, level service, expansion or reduction) that the coming budget season will follow.
watch_next: The Select Board's workshop on FY25 goals at the next Tuesday meeting, and its budget guidance from the interim town manager.
Board comments on the draft financial policy manual, due within three weeks of this meeting.
